 ECG Power Outage Schedule: Nov 15-18 Maintenance in Ashanti & Tema
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 Power cuts to hit parts of Accra, Eastern Region, Ashanti Region from 15-18: See latest schedule
 Nii Ayitey Brown
 11:00 - 15 November 2026
 An image of the official logo of the Electricity Company of Ghana and an image of a candle and a hand in the darkness depicting dumsor
 The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has scheduled emergency maintenance outages from November 15 to 18 across parts of the Ashanti region, Tema, and Eastern region to repair network technical faults and upgrade service reliability.
 Advertisement
 The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced scheduled power outages in parts of Ashanti region, Tema and Eastern region from Sunday, November 15 to Wednesday, November 18, 2026. 
 ECG says the exercise is necessary to fix faults and improve electricity reliability. 
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced emergency maintenance works following multiple faults that have recently disrupted power supply in parts of Ashanti region, Tema and Eastern region.
 READ ALSO: ECG to disconnect customers with unpaid bills and clamp down on illegal connections from Nov 9-27 
 According to ECG, the outages in affected areas are linked to technical challenges within the power distribution’s network, with maintenance works scheduled to begin in various communities.
 ECG logo
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 In a notice shared on its official social media platform X (formerly Twitter), ECG said the exercise will commence from Sunday, November 15 to November 18, between 12:00am and 4:00pm, although timelines may differ in some locations.
 Other locations will have their lights out between 8:00 am and 1:00 pm.
 READ ALSO: Power Outage to hit parts of Accra, Central and Volta Regions from Nov 9-13: Full ECG schedule 
 The power distributor explained that the temporary interruption is necessary to enable engineers carry out urgent repairs and system upgrades aimed at improving service reliability and preventing further faults.
 The exercise forms part of a series of planned and emergency maintenance operations announced in recent weeks as ECG works to stabilise electricity supply and address challenges within its distribution infrastructure.
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 Ghana’s power sector has experienced steady growth in electricity demand over the years, placing increasing pressure on transmission and distribution systems.
 Continuous investments in maintenance works, recent transformer upgrades earlier this year and network improvements remain essential to improving reliability and reducing unexpected outages.
 Mahama has also announced a 1,200MW gas power plant to overtake Akosombo as Ghana’s biggest single power facility. This initiative is intended to generate additional power for the country. 
 Russia has also agreed to work with Ghana towards establishing a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power plant to strengthen the country's electricity supply and support industrialisation.
 READ ALSO: ECG to cut power in parts of Accra and Central Region from November 2-6; See latest schedule 
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 The commitment was secured by President John Dramani Mahama during bilateral discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow.  
 The scheduled maintenance is expected to affect businesses that depend heavily on electricity during normal working hours, particularly as the outages will occur through most parts of the daytime period.
 The power distributor apologized for any inconvenience caused.
 Details of the specific schedules for affected areas have been attached below.
